title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47M in Series A
summary: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises 47 million dollars in Series A funding led by Accel and Prosus
detailed: Humyn Labs raised $47 million in a Series A funding round consisting of $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt.
The equity round was led by Accel, while Lighthouse Canton led the venture debt round.
Founded in February 2026 by Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, the startup captures human tasks in factories, warehouses, farms, and homes to train physical AI systems.
Humyn Labs reported surpassing $50 million in annualized revenue within six months of operations and plans to use funds for infrastructure and global expansion.
sentences: Humyn Labs, a physical AI research and deployment startup, has raised $47 million in a Series A funding round comprising equity and debt.

The Bengaluru-headquartered startup raised $26 million in equity funding led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence (through Bajaj Finance), Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The $21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Founded in February 2026 by Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs prepares physical AI systems for real-world deployment by translating human experience into physical understanding for robots.
The startup's proprietary capture devices record how people perform specific tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes.
Its end-to-end data engine then converts these recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion and touch.

Humyn Labs will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
“Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from.
This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand our global presence.

With a $10 billion opportunity emerging in data infrastructure, we aim to build a $1 billion annual revenue business and establish ourselves as a global leader in the space,” said Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.
According to Humyn Labs, it has surpassed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations.

It works with frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers, and runs its own capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
“A robot does not learn a job from the internet.
It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done.

We bring the model lab and the site operator onto that floor together, so every deployment teaches the next model, and the world’s factories, farms and warehouses become the training se,” said Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.
